plan.interpretation: By the end of the weekend, the learner has built and run a working habit tracker in React (Vite) that persists data to localStorage, and understands the hooks and component patterns behind it.
assumptions: Habit tracker means: add/delete habits, mark them complete per day, view streaks, with data persisted in localStorage
The 360 minutes is pure watching time, so a long project build video can serve as the backbone
Plain JavaScript (not TypeScript) is fine since the learner knows JS fundamentals but did not mention TypeScript
Modern function components and hooks only; class components are not needed
The 'nothing before 2022' constraint is handled by the later video-selection step using upload dates; the exclusions here cover title-based filters only

sub_topics.title: Vite project setup and React project structure
sub_topics.why: The learner knows npm but not Vite; they need to scaffold a modern React project and understand the folder layout, dev server and build, instead of using create-react-app.

sub_topics.title: JSX and function components with props
sub_topics.why: As a JS-literate backend dev, they need the mental model of JSX as JS expressions plus component composition and props to build UI.

sub_topics.title: State with useState and event handling
sub_topics.why: A habit tracker is driven by state (habits list, completion toggles); they need immutable updates of arrays/objects and form handling.

sub_topics.title: useEffect and persisting state to localStorage
sub_topics.why: Persistence is a core requirement; they need to understand effects, dependency arrays, lazy state initialization and JSON serialization (which they already know).

sub_topics.title: Component patterns: lifting state up, lists and keys, custom hooks
sub_topics.why: To structure a multi-component app cleanly, they need to share state between components, render lists correctly, and extract a reusable useLocalStorage hook.

sub_topics.title: Build a habit tracker / similar small app end-to-end
sub_topics.why: Following a project build ties all concepts together and mirrors the weekend goal; it is the backbone of the plan.

sub_topics.title: Streak logic, styling and finishing touches
sub_topics.why: The learner needs to adapt the tutorial project into their own habit tracker by adding date-based completion and streak calculation.

- Developers who want a lightweight, efficient alternative to traditional bundlers such as Webpack
